anomalies.observed: The LM1117-5.0 regulator U3 has its input pin VI (pin 2, with input decoupling C1) tied to the +5V net, and its output pin VO (pin 3) also tied to the +5V net. The unregulated supply net VCC (from the J6 PWR connector) is not connected to U3 at all.
anomalies.expected: A 5.0 V linear regulator must take its input from the higher, unregulated supply rail (VCC) and produce the regulated +5V at its output. Tying VI and VO to the same net leaves the regulator with no input and no dropout headroom, so the +5V rail is not actually derived from VCC.

evidence.quote: U3 LM1117-5.0: pin2 VI with C1 100nF to +5V, pin3 VO to +5V, pin1 GND (sheet /, right tile)
J6 PWR pin2 -> VCC; VCC feeds Q2 source / JP2 / R5 / C3 but not U3 (sheet /)

anomalies.impact: The +5V rail is not regulated from VCC; with VI shorted to VO the regulator is bypassed, so the MCU and +5V-side circuitry are left without a proper supply source (board fails to power up correctly, or the regulator is rendered non-functional).

parsed.summary: The drawing is largely consistent (ISP-to-ATtiny pin mapping, high-side PMOS fan switch, potentiometer on PB3, reset pull-up), but the LM1117-5.0 regulator U3 appears to have its input tied to the same +5V net as its output while the unregulated VCC rail is left unconnected to it, which would prevent the +5V rail from being properly derived from the supply.
